tasks.short: Train officers in practical dog handling

steps.what: Train police officers through dog handling demonstrations, supervised practice and feedback

tasks.design: Retain practical dog-handler training with the trainer using the approved programme in {DOCS}. The proposal does not replace demonstrations, observation of dog and handler, or corrective feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training depends on live animal behaviour and the handler's response.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approved training material supports supervised practice.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting instruction to different dog-handler combinations and judging demonstrated competence.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer observes behaviour directly and intervenes when practice needs to change.

reach.learn: Give clear feedback based on observed performance

evidence.claim: Manual practical dog-handler training is an E1 proposal; the supplied digest establishes no training replacement capability.

assumptions: The baseline is practical training rather than writing a training manual or scheduling courses.
The trainer elicits handler experience and observes dog behaviour during s1; all capture and feedback time is retained, with practice observations produced during the exercise.
No machine consumes an assumed competence or animal-readiness flag.
Existing DOCS material precedes new software; no new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Authorized training scope and current programme
research_questions: Is any repeated course administration separable from practical instruction?

already_counted.description: Demonstration, live observation, supervised practice and feedback

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. No course-writing or scheduling baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Coordinate observed training needs with police training officers
role.ambitious_version: A trainer who improves handler practice through direct observation and clear feedback
